objects.description: Opaque dictionary handle. It is a typedef to a pointer to an incomplete struct Dict_Entry, making Dict an opaque type whose head pointer may change. The actual Dict_Entry definition is not provided in this header.
Opaque list handle. It is a typedef to a pointer to an incomplete struct List_Item, allowing the list head to change. The List_Item definition is not present in this header.
String struct holding a byte buffer and its length. Length is uintptr_t; bytes is a mutable char pointer. No ownership or lifetime semantics are specified in this header.
Enumeration of the kind of value stored in an Object: integer, string, list, dictionary, or unparsable.

Tagged union value that can hold one of several types, discriminated by the type field. The union stores either a 64-bit integer, or pointers to String, List, or Dict. Memory management and construction functions are not defined in this header; users must ensure the union member matches type.

Handle representing a registered on-free callback job for an Allocator. It stores the callback function and user data; Identity expands to identity/debug fields from util/Identity.h. Jobs are created by Allocator_onFree() and can be canceled with Allocator_cancelOnFree().

Opaque allocator type for structured memory management. The concrete struct Allocator is not defined in this header; it is managed via the exposed API (create with Allocator_new or Allocator_child; free with Allocator_free; adopt with Allocator_adopt, etc.). Details of its fields are intentionally hidden.

Internal metadata structure describing a single allocation block, currently only the size field. Likely used by the allocator runtime to track allocations. The macro exposes its expected size equal to pointer size.
Function pointer type for callbacks invoked when an Allocator is being freed. The callback receives the associated Allocator_OnFreeJob.

Opaque bencoded string type used by the benc API. This header declares factory and comparison functions and provides stack-allocated convenience macros. The actual struct definition is not present here (defined elsewhere), so treat it as an opaque handle.
Opaque benc Object type referenced by the String_OBJ convenience macro. Not defined in this header; included from benc/Object.h. Ignored for construction details due to lack of definition here.
Singly linked list node used internally by the benc List type. Each node holds a pointer to the next node and an Object* payload representing a bencoded value (int, string, dict, or list).

Opaque list of bencoded objects. The full structure is not defined in this header; users manipulate it via the provided API functions (List_new, List_addInt/String/Dict/List, List_get* and List_size). Memory is managed by an Allocator passed to construction/mutation functions. Details of internal layout are intentionally hidden.

Singly linked list node representing one key/value entry in a bencoded dictionary. Each node stores a String key, an Object value, and a pointer to the next entry. Used internally by the Dict API and exposed for stack-allocated dictionary literals via Dict_CONST.

Opaque bencoded dictionary type referenced throughout this header. The concrete struct definition is not present in this header; it is defined elsewhere (likely in benc/Dict.c or another header). Provides key/value mapping of String to Object, supporting nested Dict and List values, with allocation managed via Allocator.
Opaque or externally-defined string object used as dictionary keys and values. Not defined in this header; included from other modules.

Opaque or externally-defined tagged bencode object union used to carry integers, strings, lists, and dictionaries. Not defined in this header; included from benc/Object.h. Used as the value type in Dict entries and API.
Opaque or externally-defined list type for bencoded lists. Not defined in this header; referenced by Dict get/put APIs.
Externally-defined memory allocator interface used to allocate dictionary nodes and objects. Not defined in this header; included from memory/Allocator.h.

functions.name: Allocator__malloc
functions.signature: void* Allocator__malloc(struct Allocator* allocator, unsigned long length, const char* fileName, int lineNum);
functions.description: Allocates length bytes from the given allocator. Memory is aligned at least to pointer size. Intended as the allocator-backed equivalent of malloc; the allocation is owned by the allocator and will be released when the allocator is freed.
requirements: allocator must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance.
length may be any value; alignment is at least pointer size (no further alignment is provided).
Do not free the returned pointer with free(); it is managed by the allocator.
Memory will ultimately be released by freeing the allocator or via allocator-specific mechanisms.

functions.name: Allocator_malloc
functions.signature: void* Allocator_malloc(struct Allocator* allocator, unsigned long length)
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory of the given length from the specified allocator. Alignment is at least pointer-sized. This is a convenience macro that wraps Allocator__malloc and auto-injects file/line for diagnostics. Intended as the allocator-backed equivalent of malloc().
requirements: allocator must be a valid, initialized allocator instance
length may be any value; alignment is at least sizeof(void*)
returned memory is uninitialized (not zeroed)
caller is responsible for eventually releasing memory by freeing the owning allocator or reallocating/freing the specific block via this allocator

functions.name: Allocator__calloc
functions.signature: void* Allocator__calloc(struct Allocator* alloc, unsigned long length, unsigned long count, const char* fileName, int lineNum);
functions.description: Allocates count elements of length bytes each from the allocator, with the memory zero-initialized. Alignment is at least pointer size. Allocator-backed equivalent of calloc.
requirements: alloc must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance.
length and count define total size (length * count); alignment is at least pointer size.
Do not free the returned pointer with free(); it is managed by the allocator.
Memory is zero-filled.

functions.name: Allocator_calloc
functions.signature: void* Allocator_calloc(struct Allocator* alloc, unsigned long length, unsigned long count)
functions.description: Allocates an array of count elements each of size length from the allocator, and zero-fills the resulting memory. Alignment is at least pointer-sized. This is a convenience macro wrapping Allocator__calloc with file/line capture.
requirements: alloc must be a valid, initialized allocator
length and count define the allocation size (length * count); alignment is at least sizeof(void*)
returned memory is zero-initialized
caller must manage the lifetime via the allocator (freeing the allocator or resizing/freeing via this allocator)

functions.name: Allocator__realloc
functions.signature: void* Allocator__realloc(struct Allocator* allocator, const void* original, unsigned long size, const char* fileName, int lineNum);
functions.description: Resizes or frees an existing allocation that was created by the same allocator. Behaves like realloc: if original is NULL, allocates new memory; if size is 0, frees the specific allocation. Alignment is at least pointer size. Caution: not advisable for memory shared in other parts of the system.
requirements: allocator must be the same allocator that created original when original is non-NULL.
original must be a pointer previously allocated by this allocator when non-NULL.
If original is NULL, this behaves like Allocator__malloc(allocator, size, ...).
If size is 0 and original is non-NULL, the specific allocation is freed without freeing the allocator.
Avoid using on allocations shared with other parts of the system (as noted in the caution).
Do not free returned pointers with free(); they are managed by the allocator.

functions.name: Allocator_realloc
functions.signature: void* Allocator_realloc(struct Allocator* allocator, const void* original, unsigned long size)
functions.description: Changes the size of a prior allocation made by the same allocator. If original is NULL, behaves like Allocator_malloc. If size is 0, frees the specific allocation without freeing the allocator. Alignment is at least pointer-sized. Caution: using realloc on memory shared with other parts of the system can be unsafe.
requirements: allocator must be the same allocator that created the original allocation (when original is non-NULL)
original may be NULL to perform a fresh allocation
size of 0 frees the specific allocation without destroying the allocator
returned pointer may differ from original if moved; original pointer becomes invalid after a successful resize
do not use on memory shared outside control that expects a stable pointer (as noted by the caution)

functions.name: Allocator__clone
functions.signature: void* Allocator__clone(struct Allocator* allocator, const void* toClone, unsigned long length, const char* fileName, int lineNum);
functions.description: Allocates a new block and copies length bytes from toClone into it. Alignment is at least pointer size. Equivalent to malloc(length) + memcpy, owned by the allocator.
requirements: allocator must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance.
toClone must point to at least length readable bytes.
length defines the number of bytes to copy/allocate.
Do not free the returned pointer with free(); it is managed by the allocator.

functions.name: Allocator_clone
functions.signature: void* Allocator_clone(struct Allocator* allocator, const void* toClone)
functions.description: Allocates memory and copies the object pointed to by toClone into the new allocation. The size copied is sizeof(*toClone). This is a macro over Allocator__clone that computes the length from the argument; note that if the expression passed as toClone has side effects, it will be evaluated twice.
requirements: allocator must be a valid, initialized allocator
toClone must point to a readable object whose size is sizeof(*toClone)
the expression passed as toClone should be free of side effects (it is evaluated twice)
resulting allocation has pointer-size alignment and contains a byte-for-byte copy of *toClone

functions.name: Allocator__child
functions.signature: struct Allocator* Allocator__child(struct Allocator* alloc, const char* fileName, int lineNum);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new child allocator of alloc. When a parent allocator is freed, its children that have no surviving adopted parents will also be freed.
requirements: alloc must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance.
The returned child allocator is owned hierarchically under alloc and should be freed via Allocator_free (or by freeing its parent).

functions.name: Allocator_child
functions.signature: struct Allocator* Allocator_child(struct Allocator* alloc)
functions.description: Creates a new child allocator of the given allocator. When a parent allocator is freed, all of its children that have no surviving parent are also freed. This is a macro that wraps Allocator__child with file/line capture.
requirements: alloc must be a valid, initialized allocator
callers should free their own allocators; freeing a parent will free its children without surviving parents
use child allocators instead of creating new roots where possible (per documented best practice)

functions.name: Allocator__free
functions.signature: void Allocator__free(struct Allocator* alloc, const char* file, int line);
functions.description: Severs the link between alloc and its original parent. If alloc has been adopted, freeing may be deferred until the adopted parent is also freed. Any allocator with no surviving parent will be implicitly freed. Note: This may not immediately free the allocator if it has an adopted parent.
requirements: alloc must be a valid Allocator instance.
Prefer to free only allocators that your code created (per documented guideline).
Do not assume immediate destruction if alloc has been adopted; freeing may be deferred.

functions.name: Allocator_free
functions.signature: void Allocator_free(struct Allocator* alloc)
functions.description: Severs the link between an allocator and its original parent. If the allocator has been adopted, the adopted parent becomes its effective parent and the allocator may not be immediately freed. Any allocator without a surviving parent will be implicitly freed. This is a macro wrapper over Allocator__free with file/line capture.
requirements: alloc must be a valid allocator (may be freed implicitly if it has no surviving parent)
if the allocator has been adopted, freeing it severs the normal parent link but does not necessarily free it until the adopted parent is also freed
callers should avoid freeing allocators they did not create (per documented guidance)

functions.name: Allocator_isFreeing
functions.signature: int Allocator_isFreeing(Allocator_t* alloc);
functions.description: Returns a nonzero value if the allocator is in the process of being freed; otherwise returns zero.
requirements: alloc must be a valid Allocator instance.

functions.name: Allocator__onFree
functions.signature: struct Allocator_OnFreeJob* Allocator__onFree(struct Allocator* alloc, Allocator_OnFreeCallback callback, void* context, const char* file, int line);
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked when alloc is freed. Returns a handle that can be used to cancel the callback later. Execution order of multiple onFree jobs is not guaranteed.
requirements: alloc must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called as callback(job).
The returned Allocator_OnFreeJob handle must be treated as opaque and used only with Allocator_cancelOnFree.
Do not assume any ordering among multiple registered callbacks.

functions.name: Allocator_onFree
functions.signature: struct Allocator_OnFreeJob* Allocator_onFree(struct Allocator* alloc, Allocator_OnFreeCallback callback, void* context)
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked when the allocator is freed. The order of execution among multiple onFree jobs is not guaranteed. Returns a handle that can be used to cancel the job via Allocator_cancelOnFree. This is a macro wrapping Allocator__onFree with file/line capture.
requirements: alloc must be a valid, initialized allocator
callback must be a valid function pointer of type Allocator_OnFreeCallback
context (userData) may be any pointer and will be provided to the job via job->userData
callers should not rely on the ordering of multiple onFree callbacks

functions.name: Allocator_cancelOnFree
functions.signature: int Allocator_cancelOnFree(struct Allocator_OnFreeJob* toRemove);
functions.description: Cancels a previously registered onFree job. Returns 0 if the job was found and removed; returns -1 otherwise.
requirements: toRemove must be a handle previously returned by Allocator_onFree/Allocator__onFree for some allocator.
Caller should check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates the job was not found.

functions.name: Allocator__adopt
functions.signature: void Allocator__adopt(struct Allocator* parentAlloc, struct Allocator* alloc, const char* fileName, int lineNum);
functions.description: Creates a child of parentAlloc that acts as an adopted parent of alloc. After adoption, alloc will not be freed until Allocator_free is also called on the newly created adopted parent. Can be called multiple times to add adopted parents. Caution: Do not free an allocator you did not create, even after adopting it; instead free the adopted parent you created.
requirements: parentAlloc must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance that will act as the parent for the newly created adopted parent.
alloc must be a valid Allocator instance to be adopted.
Callers should not directly free alloc if they did not create it; free the adopted parent instead (as per the documented example and caution).

functions.name: Allocator_adopt
functions.signature: void Allocator_adopt(struct Allocator* parentAlloc, struct Allocator* alloc)
functions.description: Creates a child of parentAlloc that becomes an adopted parent of alloc. After adoption, freeing alloc (or one of its parents) will be deferred until the adopted parent is also freed. May be used multiple times. This is a macro wrapping Allocator__adopt with file/line capture. Intended for transferring/holding ownership without copying.
requirements: parentAlloc must be a valid, initialized allocator
alloc must be a valid, initialized allocator to be adopted
do not free an allocator you did not create even after adopting it (as per documented caution)
free the adopted parent allocator to ultimately allow alloc to be freed

functions.name: Allocator_setCanary
functions.signature: void Allocator_setCanary(struct Allocator* alloc, uintptr_t value);
functions.description: Sets the heap protection canary value for the next child allocator. If canaries are enabled, allocations will be bookended with this value and checked to detect corruption.
requirements: alloc must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance.
value is an arbitrary uintptr_t used as the canary; effectiveness depends on canary support being enabled in the build/configuration.

functions.name: Allocator_bytesAllocated
functions.signature: unsigned long Allocator_bytesAllocated(struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes allocated by allocator and all of its children.
requirements: allocator must be a valid, initialized Allocator instance.

functions.name: Allocator_snapshot
functions.signature: void Allocator_snapshot(struct Allocator* alloc, int includeAllocations);
functions.description: Dumps a memory snapshot of the allocator tree to stderr. If includeAllocations is nonzero, individual allocations are printed.
requirements: alloc must be any valid Allocator instance in the tree to be reported.
includeAllocations is treated as a boolean flag (0 = omit individual allocations, nonzero = include them).

functions.name: Allocator__new
functions.signature: struct Allocator* Allocator__new(unsigned long sizeLimit, const char* fileName, int lineNum);
functions.description: Creates a new root allocator, optionally with a size limit. Root allocators should be rare; the typical pattern is to create child allocators from a main root. Details of sizeLimit semantics are not documented here.
requirements: Use sparingly: prefer Allocator_child over creating new root allocators, per documented guidelines.
sizeLimit constraints are unknown from this header; caller should pass an appropriate limit or 0 if unlimited is supported (unknown).
The returned allocator should be freed via Allocator_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: Allocator_new
functions.signature: struct Allocator* Allocator_new(unsigned long sizeLimit)
functions.description: Creates a new root allocator with an optional size limit. Typically there should be a single main root allocator; prefer creating child allocators for normal usage. This is a macro wrapping Allocator__new with file/line capture.
requirements: sizeLimit defines the allocator’s allocation cap (exact semantics are not documented here)
callers are responsible for eventually freeing this root allocator
prefer using Allocator_child to avoid creating additional roots unless required (e.g., certain libuv integrations)

functions.name: String_new
functions.signature: String* String_new(const char* bytes, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Create a new bencoded String from a C NUL-terminated string. The implementation copies the input bytes into memory obtained from the provided allocator. Use when you have a standard C string and want an owning bencoded String object.
requirements: bytes must point to a valid NUL-terminated C string.
allocator must be a valid Allocator capable of providing memory for the new String object and its contents.
The returned String owns an internal copy of the data; callers may free or modify the original bytes independently.

functions.name: String_newBinary
functions.signature: String* String_newBinary(const char* bytes, uintptr_t length, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Create a new bencoded String from a raw byte sequence of specified length. The implementation copies exactly length bytes into memory from the allocator. If bytes is NULL, a String of length bytes filled with NUL characters is created. Use for binary data or substrings that may contain embedded NULs.
requirements: If bytes is not NULL, it must reference at least length bytes of readable memory.
If bytes is NULL, length specifies the size of the new string (filled with NUL bytes).
length is interpreted as a byte count (may be zero).
allocator must be a valid Allocator capable of providing memory for the new String object and its contents.

functions.name: String_printf
functions.signature: String* String_printf(struct Allocator* allocator, const char* format, ...);
functions.description: Create a new bencoded String using printf-style formatting. The formatted result is copied into memory obtained from the allocator. Use when constructing strings from values using standard printf specifiers.
requirements: allocator must be a valid Allocator capable of providing memory for the new String object and its contents.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers as per the C printf contract.

functions.name: String_vprintf
functions.signature: String* String_vprintf(struct Allocator* allocator, const char* format, va_list args);
functions.description: Variant of String_printf that accepts a va_list of arguments. Only declared if stdarg.h is included before this header (va_start is defined). Use when forwarding variadic arguments.
requirements: This declaration is available only if stdarg.h is included before including String.h (va_start must be defined).
allocator must be a valid Allocator capable of providing memory for the new String object and its contents.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
args must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to format; the caller is responsible for managing va_start/va_end lifecycle.

functions.name: String_compare
functions.signature: int String_compare(const String* a, const String* b);
functions.description: Lexicographically compare two bencoded Strings. Returns negative if a < b, positive if a > b, and zero if equal. If all compared bytes are equal, returns the difference in length (a->len - b->len). Handles NULL: NULL is considered less than non-NULL; two NULLs compare equal.
requirements: a and b may be NULL; if non-NULL they must point to valid String objects.
The function imposes a total order consistent with the documented behavior; callers should not assume locale-specific collation.

functions.name: String_equals
functions.signature: int String_equals(const String* a, const String* b);
functions.description: Return nonzero if and only if String_compare(a, b) == 0, otherwise 0. Effectively tests for bytewise equality and equal length, with NULL handling identical to String_compare.
requirements: a and b may be NULL; if non-NULL they must point to valid String objects.

functions.name: List_new
functions.signature: List* List_new(struct Allocator* alloc);
functions.description: Create a new (presumably empty) list using the provided allocator. Intended as a constructor for a bencoded List object. Exact failure behavior and ownership semantics are not documented here.
requirements: allocator: a pointer to an Allocator used to obtain memory for the list (behavior if NULL is unknown).
Lifespan/ownership: unknown; ensure the allocator remains valid for at least as long as the list exists (inferred from typical allocator usage).

functions.name: List_size
functions.signature: int32_t List_size(const List* list);
functions.description: Return the number of items in the list, or -1 if the list argument is NULL. Useful to check length and to validate indices before access.
requirements: list may be NULL; in that case the function returns -1.

functions.name: List_addInt
functions.signature: void List_addInt(List* list, int64_t toAdd, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Append an integer value to the list. Documentation states that if the list does not exist (NULL) it is allocated; however, the function does not return the (possibly new) list pointer, so the exact allocation/update semantics are unclear.
requirements: allocator must provide memory for storing the list entry (and possibly for creating the list if list is NULL).
If list is NULL, documentation claims the list will be allocated; how the caller obtains the new list pointer is unspecified/unknown.
No copying concerns for the integer value (stored by value).

functions.name: List_addString
functions.signature: void List_addString(List* list, String* toAdd, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Append a string item to the list. This function does not copy the given string; it stores a pointer to it.
requirements: toAdd must point to a valid String which remains alive/unmodified as long as the list entry requires it (since the string is not copied).
allocator must provide memory for storing the list entry (and possibly for creating the list if list is NULL).
If list is NULL, documentation claims the list will be allocated; how the caller obtains the new list pointer is unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: List_addDict
functions.signature: void List_addDict(List* list, Dict* toAdd, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Append a dictionary item to the list. This function does not copy the dictionary; it stores a pointer to it.
requirements: toAdd must point to a valid Dict which remains alive/unmodified as long as the list entry requires it (since the dictionary is not copied).
allocator must provide memory for storing the list entry (and possibly for creating the list if list is NULL).
If list is NULL, documentation claims the list will be allocated; how the caller obtains the new list pointer is unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: List_addList
functions.signature: void List_addList(List* list, List* toAdd, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Append a list as an item to another list. This function does not copy the nested list; it stores a pointer to it.
requirements: toAdd must point to a valid List which remains alive/unmodified as long as the list entry requires it (since the list is not copied).
allocator must provide memory for storing the list entry (and possibly for creating the list if list is NULL).
If list is NULL, documentation claims the list will be allocated; how the caller obtains the new list pointer is unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: List_getInt
functions.signature: int64_t* List_getInt(const List* list, uint32_t index);
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to an integer at the given index. Returns NULL if the index is out of range or the item at that index is not an integer.
requirements: index must refer to a valid position within the list and the item at that position must be an integer to obtain a non-NULL result.
list should be a valid pointer to a list; behavior if NULL is that the function will return NULL (implied by out-of-range/invalid-type semantics; explicit behavior not otherwise documented).
The returned pointer remains valid as long as the underlying list/item remains alive (lifetime details not documented).

functions.name: List_getString
functions.signature: String* List_getString(const List* list, uint32_t index);
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to a string at the given index. Returns NULL if the index is out of range or the item at that index is not a string.
requirements: index must refer to a valid position within the list and the item at that position must be a string to obtain a non-NULL result.
list should be a valid pointer to a list; behavior if NULL is to return NULL (by implication; explicit behavior not otherwise documented).
The returned pointer is not owned by the caller; do not free it. Lifetime tied to the list/allocator (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: List_getDict
functions.signature: Dict* List_getDict(const List* list, uint32_t index);
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to a dictionary at the given index. Returns NULL if the index is out of range or the item at that index is not a dictionary.
requirements: index must refer to a valid position within the list and the item at that position must be a dictionary to obtain a non-NULL result.
list should be a valid pointer to a list; behavior if NULL is to return NULL (by implication; explicit behavior not otherwise documented).
The returned pointer is not owned by the caller; do not free it. Lifetime tied to the list/allocator (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: List_getList
functions.signature: List* List_getList(const List* list, uint32_t index);
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to a nested list at the given index. Returns NULL if the index is out of range or the item at that index is not a list.
requirements: index must refer to a valid position within the list and the item at that position must be a list to obtain a non-NULL result.
list should be a valid pointer to a list; behavior if NULL is to return NULL (by implication; explicit behavior not otherwise documented).
The returned pointer is not owned by the caller; do not free it. Lifetime tied to the list/allocator (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: Dict_remove
functions.signature: int32_t Dict_remove(Dict* dictionary, const String* key);
functions.description: Remove an entry from the dictionary by key. Returns 1 if an entry was removed, 0 if no matching entry existed.
requirements: dictionary: must reference a valid Dict instance. Unknown behavior if NULL (not documented).
key: must reference the key to remove; must be a valid String pointer. Unknown if NULL keys are allowed (not documented).
Caller should handle the return value: 1 means an entry was removed; 0 means no removal.

functions.name: Dict_size
functions.signature: int32_t Dict_size(const Dict* dictionary);
functions.description: Return the number of entries in the dictionary. If dictionary is NULL, returns -1.
requirements: dictionary may be NULL; function returns -1 in that case.
Caller must handle negative return value (-1) as an error/null-dictionary indicator.

functions.name: Dict_getInt
functions.signature: int64_t* Dict_getInt(const Dict* dictionary, const String* key);
functions.description: Lookup an integer value by key. Returns a pointer to the stored int64_t if present and of integer type; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: dictionary: valid Dict pointer (unknown if NULL is accepted; not documented).
key: valid String pointer corresponding to the lookup key.
Caller must check for NULL return when the key is absent or the value is not an integer.

functions.name: Dict_getIntC
functions.signature: #define Dict_getIntC(getFromHere, key) Dict_getInt(getFromHere, String_CONST(key))
functions.description: Convenience macro that looks up an integer value in a Dict using a C string key by wrapping the key with String_CONST and calling Dict_getInt. Returns the int64_t* stored under the key or NULL if absent or of the wrong type.
requirements: getFromHere must point to a valid Dict (unknown if NULL is accepted by underlying Dict_getInt).
key must be a NUL-terminated C string acceptable to String_CONST.
Caller must handle a NULL return when the key is not present or value is not an integer.

functions.name: Dict_getString
functions.signature: String* Dict_getString(const Dict* dictionary, const String* key);
functions.description: Lookup a string value by key. Returns a pointer to the stored String if present and of string type; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: dictionary: valid Dict pointer (unknown if NULL is accepted; not documented).
key: valid String pointer corresponding to the lookup key.
Caller must check for NULL return when the key is absent or the value is not a string.

functions.name: Dict_getStringC
functions.signature: #define Dict_getStringC(getFromHere, key) Dict_getString(getFromHere, String_CONST(key))
functions.description: Convenience macro that retrieves a String* from a Dict using a C string key by wrapping the key with String_CONST and calling Dict_getString. Returns the stored String* or NULL if absent or of the wrong type.
requirements: getFromHere must point to a valid Dict (unknown if NULL is accepted by underlying Dict_getString).
key must be a NUL-terminated C string acceptable to String_CONST.
Caller must handle a NULL return when the key is not present or value is not a string.

functions.name: Dict_getDict
functions.signature: Dict* Dict_getDict(const Dict* dictionary, const String* key);
functions.description: Lookup a nested dictionary value by key. Returns a Dict* if present and of dictionary type; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: dictionary: valid Dict pointer (unknown if NULL is accepted; not documented).
key: valid String pointer corresponding to the lookup key.
Caller must check for NULL return when the key is absent or the value is not a dictionary.

functions.name: Dict_getDictC
functions.signature: #define Dict_getDictC(getFromHere, key) Dict_getDict(getFromHere, String_CONST(key))
functions.description: Convenience macro that retrieves a nested Dict* from a Dict using a C string key by wrapping the key with String_CONST and calling Dict_getDict. Returns the stored Dict* or NULL if absent or of the wrong type.
requirements: getFromHere must point to a valid Dict (unknown if NULL is accepted by underlying Dict_getDict).
key must be a NUL-terminated C string acceptable to String_CONST.
Caller must handle a NULL return when the key is not present or value is not a dictionary.

functions.name: Dict_getList
functions.signature: List* Dict_getList(const Dict* dictionary, const String* key);
functions.description: Lookup a list value by key. Returns a List* if present and of list type; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: dictionary: valid Dict pointer (unknown if NULL is accepted; not documented).
key: valid String pointer corresponding to the lookup key.
Caller must check for NULL return when the key is absent or the value is not a list.

requirements: getFromHere must point to a valid Dict (unknown if NULL is accepted by underlying Dict_getList).

functions.name: Dict_putObject
functions.signature: Object* Dict_putObject(Dict* dictionary, const String* key, Object* value, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Insert or replace an entry in the dictionary with the given Object value under key. Returns the previously stored value if the key existed, otherwise NULL. Allocation for the entry wrapper uses the provided allocator.
requirements: dictionary: must be a valid Dict pointer prepared for insertion.
key: must be a valid String pointer used as the dictionary key.
value: must be a valid Object pointer. Ownership/retention semantics are not documented; assumed stored by pointer (unknown whether copied).
allocator: must be a valid Allocator pointer used to allocate storage for the entry metadata.

functions.name: Dict_putInt
functions.signature: Object* Dict_putInt(Dict* putIntoThis, const String* key, int64_t value, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Insert an integer value under key. Returns the displaced value if the key already existed, otherwise NULL. Uses allocator for the entry wrapper.
requirements: putIntoThis: valid Dict pointer.
key: valid String pointer to use as the reference key.
value: any int64_t value is acceptable (no range restrictions beyond int64_t).
allocator: valid Allocator pointer.
Caller must check the return value to handle any displaced Object (non-NULL indicates a previous value was replaced).

functions.name: Dict_putIntC
functions.signature:
#define Dict_putIntC(putHere, key, val, alloc) \
    Dict_putInt(putHere, String_new(key, alloc), val, alloc)
functions.description: Convenience macro that inserts an integer into a Dict using a C string key by constructing a String via String_new and calling Dict_putInt. Returns the displaced Object* if the key already exists, otherwise NULL.
requirements: putHere must point to a valid Dict.
key must be a NUL-terminated C string acceptable to String_new.
val is the integer value to store (int64_t).
alloc must be a valid Allocator* for creating the String key and dictionary entry wrapper.
Caller must handle the return which may be a displaced Object* or NULL.

functions.name: Dict_putString
functions.signature: Object* Dict_putString(Dict* putIntoThis, const String* key, String* value, struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Insert a String object under key. The function does not copy the String; it stores the pointer in the dictionary. Returns the displaced value if the key already existed, otherwise NULL.
requirements: putIntoThis: valid Dict pointer.
key: valid String pointer to use as the reference key.
value: valid String pointer. The value is not copied; the caller must ensure the String remains valid for as long as it is stored in the dictionary or until it is removed (inferred from the note).
allocator: valid Allocator pointer.
Caller must check the return value to handle any displaced Object.

functions.name: Dict_putStringC
functions.signature:
#define Dict_putStringC(putHere, key, val, alloc) \
    Dict_putString(putHere, String_new(key, alloc), val, alloc)
functions.description: Convenience macro that inserts a String object into a Dict using a C string key by constructing a String via String_new and calling Dict_putString. The value is not copied; only the pointer is stored. Returns the displaced Object* if any, otherwise NULL.
requirements: putHere must point to a valid Dict.
key must be a NUL-terminated C string acceptable to String_new.
val must be a valid String*; it is stored by pointer and not copied.
alloc must be a valid Allocator* for creating the String key and entry wrapper.
Caller must handle the return which may be a displaced Object* or NULL.

functions.name: Dict_putStringCC
functions.signature:
#define Dict_putStringCC(putHere, key, val, alloc) \
    Dict_putStringC(putHere, key, String_new(val, alloc), alloc)
functions.description: Convenience macro that inserts a C string as a String object into a Dict using a C string key. It constructs the value String with String_new and delegates to Dict_putStringC. The value is not copied beyond the String object created. Returns the displaced Object* if any, otherwise NULL.
requirements: putHere must point to a valid Dict.
key must be a NUL-terminated C string acceptable to String_new.
val must be a NUL-terminated C string acceptable to String_new to construct the value String.
alloc must be a valid Allocator* for creating both key and value String objects and the entry wrapper.
Caller must handle the return which may be a displaced Object* or NULL.

functions.name: Dict_new
functions.signature: Dict* Dict_new(struct Allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Create a new bencoded dictionary using the provided allocator.
requirements: allocator: must be a valid Allocator pointer capable of allocating memory for the dictionary.

functions.name: Dict_CONST
functions.signature:
#define Dict_CONST(entryKey, value, nextDict) \
    (&(struct Dict_Entry) {                   \
        .key = entryKey,                      \
        .val = value,                         \
        .next = nextDict                      \
    })
functions.description: Macro to create a dictionary node on the stack using a compound literal. It produces a pointer to a Dict_Entry that links a key and value, and can be chained via nextDict to build a temporary dictionary structure.
requirements: entryKey must be a String* (per comment: the key must be a string).
value must be an Object* (per comment: the value must be an object).
nextDict must be another Dict (pointer) created via Dict_CONST or NULL to terminate the chain.
The returned pointer refers to a stack-allocated compound literal and is only valid within the lifetime/scope where the macro is used; do not use it after the creating scope ends.

functions.name: Dict_OBJ
functions.signature: #define Dict_OBJ(x) (&(Object) { .type = Object_DICT, .as.dictionary = x })
functions.description: Macro that wraps a Dict* as an Object of type Object_DICT using a compound literal and returns a pointer to that Object. Useful when an Object* is required from an existing Dict*.
requirements: x must be a Dict* to be assigned to the Object's dictionary union member.
The returned pointer refers to a stack-allocated compound literal and is only valid within the lifetime/scope where the macro is used; do not use it after the creating scope ends.

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated ASCII/byte string suitable for passing as const char*. May contain any bytes except it must include a terminating NUL at the end. Used for filenames, format strings, and dictionary keys where APIs expect const char*.
An arbitrary sequence of bytes with an explicit length; may include embedded NULs. Used when APIs accept (const void*, length) or raw buffers without requiring NUL-termination.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: C string (NUL-terminated). Used by many stubs as const char* via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Goal: Provide interesting yet valid NUL-terminated strings that exercise different code paths:
# - Filenames (with paths, extensions, edge names)
# - Format strings (printf specifiers)
# - Small/large strings, empty string, unicode-ish bytes, embedded NUL not allowed (so only terminate at end)
# - Keys commonly used in dicts
# - Text that looks like numbers
# - Repeated characters, mixed cases, unusual but valid ASCII
# - Reasonable length cap well under 4096 bytes
#
# The fuzzer framework will request multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values from a single buffer.
# A common pattern is to encode multiple NUL-terminated strings concatenated together.
# We'll therefore generate a sequence of such C strings, each terminated by \0, concatenated.
# The fuzzer runtime will consume them in order. This keeps all requests satisfied with valid data.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_KEYS = [
    "id", "name", "type", "value", "count", "size", "parent", "child",
    "list", "dict", "string", "int", "status", "error", "line", "file",
    "allocator", "owner", "adopted_parents", "created_by"
]

FILENAMES = [
    "",  # empty
    ".", "..",
    "a", "A", "0",
    "tmp.txt", "data.bin", "image.jpeg", "log", "Makefile",
    "path/with/slash", "./relative/path", "../up/one", "/abs/path/file",
    "weird.name.with.many.dots.ext", "spaces in name.txt", "unicode_like.txt",
]

FORMAT_STRINGS = [
    "%s", "%d", "%lld", "%u", "%x", "%p", "%zu", "%08x",
    "[%s] %d:%s", "%s %s %s", "%.*s", "%1$d %2$s %3$lld",
]

NUMERIC_STRINGS = [
    "0", "1", "-1", "42", "-9223372036854775808", "9223372036854775807",
    "18446744073709551615",  # large unsigned
]

MIXED_INTERESTING = [
    "key", "value", "K", "V",
    "alpha", "BETA", "Gamma123", "kebab-case", "snake_case",
    "CamelCase", "UPPER_lower_MIXED", "with\tescapes", "with spaces",
]

EXTENSIONS = [".txt", ".bin", ".dat", ".cfg", ".json", ".c", ".h", ".log"]

# Build some random but printable ASCII without NUL inside, to keep entire cstring valid.
def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # printable plus some punctuation; exclude '\x00' obviously
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    # Remove '%' sometimes to avoid accidental format spec issues for general strings
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    return s

# Build filename-like string
def rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 50% choose from preset
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = rng.choice(FILENAMES)
    else:
        parts = []
        depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
        for _ in range(depth):
            part = ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-", k=rng.randint(1, 8)))
            parts.append(part)
        name = ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-", k=rng.randint(1, 12)))
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            name += rng.choice(EXTENSIONS)
        path = '/'.join(parts + [name]) if parts else name
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            path = '/' + path
        base = path
    return base

# Build printf-like format sometimes, else a random ascii string
def rand_format_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(FORMAT_STRINGS)
    # create a string with some % sprinkled
    s = rand_ascii(rng, 5, 20)
    # insert a few format tokens safely
    tokens = ["%s", "%d", "%x", "%%", "%llu"]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
        tok = rng.choice(tokens)
        s = s[:pos] + tok + s[pos:]
    return s

# Build dictionary-like keys
def rand_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(COMMON_KEYS)
    modes = [
        lambda: ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=rng.randint(1, 12))),
        lambda: ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-", k=rng.randint(1, 16))),
        lambda: 'key_' + str(rng.randint(0, 10000)),
    ]
    return rng.choice(modes)()

# Build an aggregate list of C strings based on expected consumption in stubs.
# We include enough to cover: filenames, keys, values, format strings, general strings.

def build_cstrings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    items: List[bytes] = []

    # Some deterministic corner cases first
    corner_cases = [
        b"\x00",  # empty string
        b"0\x00",
        b"-1\x00",
        b"true\x00",
        b"false\x00",
        b"null\x00",
    ]
    items.extend(corner_cases)

    # Filenames
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        s = rand_filename(rng).encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        items.append(s)

    # Format strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        s = rand_format_like(rng).encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        items.append(s)

    # Dict keys
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        s = rand_key(rng).encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        items.append(s)

    # Values: include numbers-as-strings and random ascii
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = rng.choice(NUMERIC_STRINGS)
        else:
            s = rng.choice(MIXED_INTERESTING)
        items.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00")

    # Some larger payloads for clone/calloc/malloc diagnostics strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        s = rand_ascii(rng, 64, 256).encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        items.append(s)

    # A very long string near the cap (not exceeding MAX_TOTAL once concatenated). We'll adjust later.
    long_len = rng.randint(512, 1200)
    long_str = (''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_./", k=long_len))).encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
    items.append(long_str)

    # A few random short ones
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 15)):
        s = rand_ascii(rng, 1, 24).encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        items.append(s)

    return items


def pack_items(items: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate items up to MAX_TOTAL bytes, ensuring each item ends with a single NUL.
    out = bytearray()
    for it in items:
        # Ensure it contains exactly one terminating NUL at the end
        if not it or it[-1:] != b"\x00":
            it = it.rstrip(b"\x00") + b"\x00"
        # If adding would exceed MAX_TOTAL, stop
        if len(out) + len(it) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += it
    # Ensure non-empty and ends with NUL
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x00")
    elif out[-1] != 0:
        out += b"\x00"
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    items = build_cstrings(rng)
    buf = pack_items(items)
    return buf
